nodes.label: Framework decision: Next.js 16 App Router (CONFIRMED)
nodes.rationale: Covers marketing site and admin in one app/repo (single-repo requirement), builds on existing Next.js experience (most important for a solo project), and gives SSR/SSG/ISR plus strong SEO defaults.

nodes.label: Rendering strategy per page type (SSG/ISR/SSR)
nodes.rationale: Static marketing pages SSG; courses/videos/downloads ISR every few hours; blog ISR ~10-30 min; admin SSR behind auth; forms client component + server action/API route.

nodes.label: Server Components + Server Actions data fetching
nodes.rationale: Server Components fetch directly via Prisma (no internal API layer for the frontend); forms submit to Server Actions writing to Lead with no email notification; admin uses Server Actions/Components behind session checks. Keeps business logic reachable as a future mobile API surface.

nodes.label: Upload security checklist (10 mandatory server-side checks)
nodes.rationale: Local disk lacks managed-object-store protections, so: auth first, type allowlist not blocklist, magic-byte verification, re-encode images via jimp, max file size, random filenames, store/serve with no execute permission, rate limit, malware scan if feasible, log every upload. Applies uniformly — public-facing files are the higher-risk case.

nodes.label: Local-disk media storage (persistent Docker volume)
nodes.rationale: Named volume mounted at /app/uploads or files are lost on every rebuild; nginx serving statically is recommended; back up the volume with Postgres. Paths are plain strings so a later S3/R2/MinIO migration needs no schema change.

nodes.label: Performance targets (Lighthouse ≥ 90 mobile, lazy Aparat embeds)
nodes.rationale: Mobile-first testing at ~360-414px; self-hosted Vazirmatn via next/font/local; Aparat embeds lazy-loaded because the current WP site loads them eagerly.
